articles.title: Week 8 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Lineup Advice and Smart Sleepers to Exploit
articles.summary: We've reached the midway point of most fantasy-football seasons. Week 8 will bring a pivotal schedule for most managers, and it will get underway with Thursday night's matchup between the Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
We've reached the midway point of most fantasy-football seasons. Week 8 will bring a pivotal schedule for most managers, and it will get underway with Thursday night's matchup between the Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers.

At this point in the season, managers rarely have all of their top draft choices available because of injuries. This year has seen a cascade of significant injuries, and managers will also have to deal with the Houston Texans, New Orleans Saints, New York Giants, and San Francisco 49ers being on bye.

Here, you'll find some early start/sit recommendations for second-tier stars in Week 8. You'll also find a quick rundown of some sleepers who may be available on the waiver wire.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Start: Josh Jacobs, RB, Green Bay Packers

Josh Jacobs made his 2026 debut for the Packers on Sunday after being removed from the commissioner's exempt list.

Any managers concerned that Green Bay would ease him back onto the field need not have worried. He didn't exactly impress as a runner, averaging just 3.3 yards per carry against the Detroit Lions. However, he was heavily involved in the offense and finished with five catches, 91 scrimmage yards, and a touchdown.

Jacobs should maintain a significant backfield role moving forward, as no other back on the roster has been steadily efficient this season running the ball. He's one of the league's better receiving backs, and he has a terrific matchup this week against the Panthers.

Carolina has surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing running backs in 2026 and was just gashed for 258 rushing yards by the Green Bay Packers.

Sit: Zach Charbonnet, RB, Seattle Seahawks

The Seattle Seahawks may ease Zach Charbonnet into the lineup if they decide to play him in Week 8 at all. Seattle designated the bruising ball-carrier for return from last year's ACL tear and initially listed him as questionable before ruling him out for Week 7 over the weekend.

The Seahawks instead leaned on Emanuel Wilson, who had a 100-yard game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday night. Even if Charbonnet is healthy and gets the start, Wilson should see a sizeable role next Monday against the Chicago Bears.

The Bears will be coming off a long week after playing last Thursday, and they've really started to tighten up their run defense. They have surrendered the eighth-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs this season.

Charbonnet is rostered in 65 percent of fantasy leagues and is worth scooping up for future use if available. However, managers should not plan to play him against Chicago.

Start: Omar Cooper Jr., WR, New York Jets

The New York Jets lost to the previously winless Miami Dolphins on Sunday, which is obviously a disappointment. However, rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. did anything but disappoint for the Jets.

Cooper caught five passes for 115 yards and a touchdown against Miami and finished with more than 22 fantasy points for the second straight week. The Indiana product has quickly become one of Geno Smith's favorite targets, and he should maintain that role against the Las Vegas Raiders this week.

The Raiders have been a middle-of-the-road defense against opposing receivers this season, surrendering an average of 26.6 fantasy points to opposing receiver groups.

While Cooper is quickly rocketing away from sleeper status, he's still only rostered in 39 percent of fantasy leagues. He's a must-add if available, and he's worth a flex start in Week 8.

Sit: Courtland Sutton, WR, Denver Broncos

The Denver Broncos looked a little better offensively during Sunday's win over the Arizona Cardinals. However, they also lost receiver Jaylen Waddle to a chest injury on a poorly executed designed run.

With Waddle's status unclear, one might expect to see a big opportunity for fellow Broncos receiver Courtland Sutton. However, the offense still isn't clicking to a degree where it's comfortable starting Sutton in a tough matchup.

Denver was able to open things up a bit with Bo Nix against Arizona, and Sutton still finished with a modest three catches and 45 yards. He still has not recorded double-digit fantasy points in a game this season.

Sutton won't have an easy time breaking the trend against the Kansas City Chiefs, either. Kansas City has surrendered the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers. Sutton delivered just 3.1 points the last time these AFC West rivals faced off.

Other Sleepers to Exploit Off the Waiver Wire

Antonio Williams, WR, Washington Commanders

Chigoziem Okonkwo, TE, Washington Commanders

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Ranking Best Trade Assets on NFL's Worst Teams After Week 7
articles.summary: With the 2026 NFL trade deadline fast approaching, it's the perfect time to highlight some of the top assets on the teams most likely to be sellers over the next two weeks.
articles.body:
With the 2026 NFL trade deadline fast approaching, it's the perfect time to highlight some of the top assets on the teams most likely to be sellers over the next two weeks.

Over a third of the league has two or fewer wins going into Week 8. These clubs are the most likely candidates to ship off veterans—especially those on the final year of their respective contracts—in exchange for draft picks and younger talents.

Some two-win teams do still have a glimmer of hope due to their placement in a weak division, with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and New Orleans Saints both still very much alive in the NFC South. The Houston Texans aren't ready to throw in the towel either, having made the bold decision to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr. despite a slow start. These squads were left off the list.

With that in mind, let's take a ranked look (based on the expected value they would return in a trade) at the best trade assets each of the projected deadline sellers has available.

The Arizona Cardinals stunned both Los Angeles teams this season, but haven't beaten any of their other five opponents.

They are well out of contention going into Week 8, an unsurprising place for a team in Year 1 of a rebuild under a new regime to find itself.

The 2026 trade deadline represents an optimal time for Arizona to offload some aging veterans and add more picks to its arsenal.

The Cardinals re-added Lopez to their roster at the start of the offseason, but they could be ready to move on from him again by the midpoint of the 2026 campaign.

While the 29-year-old is having a decent year (21 tackles, three tackles for a loss and one sack), his age and short-term contract aren't congruent with Arizona's trajectory.

Lopez, who was a regular starter for the Cards in 2023-24, inked a modest two-year, $10.5 million contract with Arizona after spending one season with the Detroit Lions.

He's a decent trade option for any championship hopeful seeking to bolster the teeth of a defense.

Baker has been a foundational piece of the Cardinals' defense for the last decade, but the eight-time Pro Bowler could finally be on his way out of the desert after flirting with an exit several times in recent years.

Although he still looks effective as ever in his increasingly versatile role—especially as a pass-rusher, where he has already notched a career-high 3.5 sacks this season—he's on the wrong side of 30 and could be best used by this rebuilding franchise as a trade chip.

Plenty of teams will have interest in a player of Baker's caliber if he's made available.

After winning a Super Bowl with the Philadelphia Eagles two years ago, Sweat became the crown jewel of Arizona's 2025 free-agent class.

While he delivered with 12 sacks in his first year with the club, the firing of head coach Jonathan Gannon (Sweat's defensive coordinator in Philly) has had a negative impact on the edge-rusher's performance.

Given he still has two seasons left on his four-year, $76.4 million deal, has regressed to record just two sacks in seven games and doesn't have strong ties to new coach Mike LaFleur, the organization shouldn't hesitate to flip the 29-year-old for draft picks.

The Indianapolis Colts made the brash choice to run it back in 2026 with largely the same core from last year's team.

That decision has backfired spectacularly and the collapse has led to speculation that the franchise, which already fired general manager Chris Ballard, will blow things up and amass capital at the trade deadline.

Buckner is in the late stages of a fantastic NFL career, but he could finish out his third act with a different franchise.

The defensive tackle has been a force since joining the Colts in 2020, putting together two of his three Pro Bowl seasons and earning his lone first-team All-Pro nod.

Because Buckner still has plenty left in the tank—evidenced by his four sacks (matching last year's total) in seven games—he should be a popular player for rival franchises to inquire about.

The 32-year-old no longer aligns with the Colts' trajectory and is playing out the string on an expiring contract, making him one of the top trade candidates on a roster loaded with them.

Teams in the market for a premium running back should look no further than Taylor. Although his efficiency has slightly declined during this lost season, he's still at the peak of his powers.

The 27-year-old has amassed 765 yards and eight touchdowns from scrimmage, sticking out as one of the few bright spots on this downtrodden roster.

While it did seem that Taylor would be sticking around for several more seasons after agreeing to a two-year, $44 million extension just a few months ago, the rapid development of promising backup Seth McGowan could influence a pivot towards a full-blown rebuild in Indianapolis.

Multiple teams have reportedly already expressed interest in Taylor, who could return a significant package of picks and young players for his services.

Nelson is a generational guard who still has plenty left to offer NFL teams. He's more than lived up to the hype surrounding his selection at No. 6 overall in the 2018 draft, going on to make the Pro Bowl in each of his first eight seasons.

He has rarely missed time (playing in 136 games, all starts, since coming out of Notre Dame) and remains a force in the offensive trenches during an age-30 campaign.

Nelson is on an expiring contract, though, which does up the chances that Indy decides to make the once unthinkable decision to trade him.

His presence would have a transformative effect on any offensive line he joins. There are several contenders who have a clear need for a guard upgrade, making a bidding war a distinct possibility should the Colts elect to part ways with one of the greatest interior offensive linemen of the era.

After seven weeks of play to open the 2026 season, the Los Angeles Chargers stand alone as the NFL's only winless team.

It's been a head-scratching fall for a franchise that had opened the Jim Harbaugh era with back-to-back playoff berths, one that should prompt a slew of changes both leading up to the trade deadline and during the upcoming 2027 offseason.

James has consistently ranked as one of the best players on L.A.'s roster over the last eight seasons, putting the injury woes of his early career behind him and emerging as a perennial Pro Bowler. While he's a consistent force and leader for the Chargers' defense, he's also in an age-30 campaign and playing on a pricy three-year, $75.6 million extension signed this offseason.

There should be no shortage of interest in James' elite playmaking abilities. The safety has racked up 705 tackles, 19 sacks, 12 interceptions, six forced fumbles and three fumble recoveries since entering the league and should have plenty left in the tank to help a contender make multiple Super Bowl runs in the coming few seasons.

While teams don't usually ship off effective defenders who are still on their rookie contracts, the Bolts could break the mold with Tuipulotu.

Despite being just 24 years old and establishing himself as one of the league's better up-and-coming edge-rushers over the last two seasons, the door is open for a potential split.

L.A. failed to negotiate an extension with the 2023 second-rounder this summer, making it a very real possibility that Tuipulotu exits in free agency.

Rather than risk losing him in free agency for only a potential 2028 compensatory pick, the Chargers have to at least consider trading him for a premium pick at the deadline.

Mack is one of his generation's best edge-rushers, but even he hasn't been able to will Los Angeles to a victory in 2026.

Rather than waste the twilight of his esteemed career on a team trending towards the No. 1 overall pick, the Bolts should be willing to let Mack chase a ring while picking up some draft capital for their trouble.

With Mack playing on a one-year, $18 million contract, there isn't much incentive for a Chargers team on the cusp of a full-blown rebuild to retain the 35-year-old.

Shipping him off while his value remains high (Mack has a trio of sacks in six games) would benefit both sides here.

Predicting Five Potential Shocking Trades 😲

The Miami Dolphins finally got into the win column in Week 7, but that victory isn't close to enough to convince anyone this team should be anything more than sellers at the trade deadline.

The 'Phins should be stockpiling capital with an eye towards a loaded 2027 NFL draft class.

Teams are always looking to reinforce the offensive trenches at this time of year and 2026 shouldn't be any different. While Jackson is having a rough go of things in Miami (rating as Pro Football Focus ' lowest-graded offensive tackle), a change of scenery could rejuvenate the veteran.

Jackson has a first-round pedigree and is playing out the final year of his contract. His recent form and injury history are concerning, but teams looking for an experienced option at the tackle position won't find much better on the trade market.

Uche is a mildly productive edge rusher who could be far more valuable in a Super Bowl contender's pass-rushing rotation than starting for the struggling 'Phins. He's recorded 25 tackles and a sack on the year, but at the age of 28 and playing on a one-year deal, there isn't much reason for Miami to keep him around.

Uche's best campaign came in 2022, a year he totaled 11.5 sacks for the New England Patriots. He hasn't eclipsed three sacks in a season since, but contenders could gamble a late-round draft pick on that ceiling.

Brooks is the most valuable trade chip the Dolphins have right now. He's under contract through the 2029 season after signing a three-year, $48 million extension this offseason—a reasonable price for an elite off-ball linebacker still in his prime.

Brooks has racked up 52 tackles this season. While it's off the pace from his league-leading 183-tackle campaign in 2025, it's still an impressive contribution given Miami's inadequacy at several other key defensive positions. He could slot in and start for plenty of Lombardi Trophy hopefuls and could command a Day 2 pick for those services.

It's time for the Philadelphia Eagles to prioritize the future.

Their outlook worsened when news emerged that star quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season after being diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs.

Philadelphia is now 2-5 after five consecutive losses. Even if a division title remains within reach, the Eagles should consider selling at the trade deadline.

The acquisition of Woolen was a gamble that didn't pay off for the Eagles.

Coming off a Super Bowl victory with the Seattle Seahawks, he earned a one-year, $12 million contract in free agency. He's since regressed to the worst version of himself, conceding a career-high 13.6 yards per attempt in coverage and giving up two touchdowns in just six games.

Despite the downturn, Woolen is still an athletic, skilled 6'4" cornerback with championship experience. He'll have opportunities to turn things around elsewhere, potentially as early as this coming week if the Eagles opt to trade him.

Ojomo should be one of the year's more coveted trade candidates. Despite playing along one of the league's more talented defensive lines, the 25-year-old blossomed last year—recording the first six sacks of his career to go along with 38 tackles.

With Philly unlikely to be able to afford keeping a backup defensive tackle at the price Ojomo is expected to command on the open market, it makes sense to flip him for picks.

Plenty of aspiring champions could use a versatile, talented 6'3", 292-pound tackle to shore up the defensive trenches.

Just over a year ago, it would have been unthinkable for the Eagles to consider moving on from Saquon Barkley.

The star running back rejuvenated his career after landing with the club in 2024, racking up more than 2,000 yards on the ground and powering the club to a Super Bowl victory.

A trade now seems far more possible, as a slight regression—coupled with an increase in contract value and some injury woes—has opened the door for a breakup.

The Eagles shouldn't rush to trade Barkley (who still has two more seasons left on his current deal), but a strong offer from a team that feels it is a feature back away from winning it all could convince management it's the right time to part ways.

Despite getting off the schneid in Week 6, the Tennessee Titans wasted no time stumbling again in a Week 7 loss.

With their status as a non-contender secure, expect the Titans to host a fire sale leading up to the trade deadline.

Johnson is one of Tennessee's newest players, having only joined in March after the club flipped T'Vondre Sweat to the New York Jets for his services.

The edge-rusher could be on the move for the second time in just over half of a year, as his blend of steady production and age makes him a tantalizing asset for Super Bowl candidates.

While Johnson is on the last year of his rookie deal—playing the 2026 campaign on the $13.4 million fifth-year option Gang Green exercised on his contract—he should still command a decent return as teams look to not only rent him for a playoff run but also see if he fits in their system ahead of his first free-agency foray.

Hooker is a solid trade target for any team seeking an experienced safety to round out their secondary. He's proven to be dependable across his seven-plus NFL seasons, starting 73 games in that span while recording 462 tackles, 42 pass defenses and 14 interceptions.

While Hooker isn't a Pro Bowl-caliber talent, he's the type of quality starter championship squads can lean on to stabilize a defense. He's also under contract through the 2028 campaign at an average of $13.5 million per year, providing extended team control to whichever club winds up with him at the deadline.

Simmons should be the most popular trade target on a Tennessee roster chock-full of candidates. He's one of the better interior defensive linemen in the league right now, having earned Pro Bowl nods in four of the past five seasons and emerging as an All-Pro in 2025.

With the ability to both shut down the run and create pressure from his defensive tackle position, Simmons is the type of do-it-all centerpiece that a team can build its front around. He's averaged nearly 52 tackles and six sacks per season over his seven-plus years in the league, achieving a career-high of 11 sacks to go along with an impressive 67 tackles in 2025.

Expect Simmons, who is under contract through 2030 after signing a three-year, $105.8 million extension in June, to net the Titans a hefty return on the trade market. A first-round pick plus potentially more could be coming Tennessee's way if brass elects to deal him at the deadline.

The Washington Commanders went into their Week 7 bye on the heels of yet another disheartening loss.

By dropping to 1-4-1 and losing star wideout Terry McLaurin in the same contest, this long-suffering franchise is well on its way to yet another disappointing campaign.

Sweeping changes are needed to turn things around, a process that could begin in earnest at the deadline.

Chaisson has one defining trait that makes him an asset at the NFL level: the ability to put pressure on opposing quarterbacks.

While his run defense is lacking, he will still be on the radar of many contending franchises thanks to his penchant for disruption in the backfield.

The 27-year-old has played for four different franchises over the past four seasons and could join a fifth if the right offer comes along. He has 2.5 sacks in six games and could bolster the edge-rushing rotation of several contenders.

A one-year, $11.5 million deal gives little incentive for Washington to retain Chaisson for the remainder of this lost season.

Robertson has been one of the few bright spots for Washington's defense this year, delivering better-than-expected results on the two-year deal he signed as a free agent.

He's proved himself to be a versatile corner who can play multiple positions in the secondary, an asset that will make him a popular trade candidate leading up to the deadline.

Payne has been a key part of Washington's defensive efforts for the better part of the last decade, but he's on an expiring contract and is far from guaranteed to return in 2027.

Because he's still playing at a high level—recording a solid 17 pressures and a sack in six games—he should draw a lot of interest from contending squads seeking to beef up in the defensive trenches.

While Payne has struggled to put up big numbers before and after his lone Pro Bowl season in 2022 (a campaign in which he recorded a career-best 11.5 sacks), he's consistently made his presence felt via pressure on the passer and run-stuffing at the line of scrimmage.

Washington shouldn't have much trouble getting a decent pick or promising young player in return for Payne.

articles.title: DJ Moore mansion: Inside $5M, 10,000 sq ft North Carolina home of Buffalo Bills wide receiver listed after Chicago Bears trade
articles.summary: DJ Moore bought the North Carolina mansion during his fifth season with the Carolina Panthers.
articles.body: DJ Moore bought the North Carolina mansion during his fifth season with the Carolina Panthers. The franchise selected him in the first round of the 2018 NFL Draft as their 24th overall pick.He joined the Chicago Bears in 2023. He played two seasons for them through 2025. The Chicago Bears then traded him to the Buffalo Bills in the 2026 offseason.After the blockbuster deal, the 29-year-old wide receiver listed his luxurious North Carolina mansion for $5.225 million in July 2026. The waterfront property is located near Charlotte and has three levels of living space. Let’s learn more about it.DJ Moore’s North Carolina mansion detailsDJ Moore’s luxurious estate is situated in the gated Sanctuary at Lake Wylie community on the outskirts of Charlotte, North Carolina. It covers nearly 10,000 sq. ft. of living space across a four-acre plot.The property was built in 2019. It features five bedrooms, five full bathrooms, a two-story foyer, hardwood floors, custom millwork, and nearly 340 ft of shoreline along Lake Wylie.The beautiful location offers scenic waterfront views. The gated community provides shared amenities like a swimming pool, tennis courts, and walking trails.The $5 million-worth abode features spacious interiors with entertainment and wellness facilities. It boasts 12-foot ceilings, French oak flooring, and expansive glass walls that offer scenic views of the surrounding grounds and lake.The gourmet kitchen comes with an eat-in island and a breakfast nook. The kitchen also features top-tier appliances, integrated refrigerator, a six-burner Wolf range, and two dishwashers.It boasts a separate scullery that serves as preparation space. The kitchen also boasts backlit Cristallo Quartzite countertops and a large bar for entertaining, as per Mansion Global. The kitchen leads to a screened-in porch and offers additional space to enjoy the waterfront view.DJ Moore’s Lake Wylie mansion in CharlotteThe primary suite features custom closets and a spa-like bathroom with a soaking tub, dual vanities, and an oversized dual-entry rain shower. The primary suite has its own private balcony.The estate also includes a separate glam powder room and two laundry rooms. Outside, the estate features a heated saltwater swimming pool, an outdoor kitchen, and access to a sandy beach.A theatre-ready room, wellness/yoga space, and exercise area enhance the estate’s appeal on the lower level. A pair of garages can accommodate up to four vehicles. A detached garage has an unfinished area above it that could be used as a guest room, office, or studio, depending on the owner’s needs.According to Mansion Global, the NFL wide receiver purchased the luxurious abode for $5 million in June 2022. It was initially listed for the same $5 million in 2024. But it was relisted for $5.225 million in July 2026.However, only recently, the asking price was dropped back to its purchase price - $5 million. Despite its expansive grounds and luxurious amenities, the property has remained unsold for over two years now.DJ Moore praises Bills’ offense and Keon ColemanDJ Moore was traded from the Chicago Bears to the Buffalo Bills in the 2026 offseason. But he suffered a grade 1 AC joint sprain in his left shoulder in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season against the Detroit Lions.He missed Week 3 and returned in Week 4. Unfortunately, he aggravated the injury during Week 4 vs. the New England Patriots. He missed Week 5 vs. the Los Angeles Rams and Week 6 vs. the Las Vegas Raiders.He will use his Week 7 bye to rest and recover further. Head coach Joe Brady feels Moore could return in Week 8 vs. the Baltimore Ravens.Moore recently spoke on WGR 550 sports radio reacting to the Buffalo Bills’ offense without him. The 29-year-old Maryland alum believes the offense has gained confidence after winning games during his absence.He believes every victory strengthens the team’s confidence and builds the players’ momentum as they move through the season. He already had confidence in the team’s abilities, but the recent successes have further boosted his belief.Keon Coleman, who was a trade subject/draft debate in the 2025 season and even 2026 offseason, stepped up in Moore’s absence. Moore praised Coleman for his consistency, work ethic, and development.According to Moore, Coleman comes to work every day with the same personality and enthusiasm. He remains committed to improving his game.Moore highlighted Coleman’s dedication to studying his playbook, asking questions, and applying what he learns on Sundays. articles.title: Can Tom Brady really say that? His blunt referee criticism on FOX is testing the limits of an NFL owner’s leash
articles.summary: Tom Brady spent much of Sunday's Packers-Lions broadcast questioning flags, and it put an old issue back in front of the NFL.
articles.body: Tom Brady spent much of Sunday's Packers-Lions broadcast questioning flags, and it put an old issue back in front of the NFL. Brady is FOX's lead NFL analyst. He also owns a piece of the Las Vegas Raiders, and that comes with limits on how hard he can criticize officials. Detroit won 20–17, but the penalties took over the conversation. Roughing calls against Green Bay for hits on Jared Goff drew his sharpest reaction. As of Monday, no punishment has been announced, FOX declined to comment, and the NFL had not immediately responded.Tom Brady's officiating criticism and the line the NFL set for himThe issue is not that Tom Brady disagreed with the officials. Analysts do that every Sunday. What makes his case different is the Raiders stake, and Front Office Sports reporter Mark Maske laid out how the league treats it once the broadcast started drawing attention."The NFL's restrictions on Brady, stemming from his role as a Raiders part-owner, include a limitation on how far he can go in criticizing the officiating. It's subjective," Maske wrote."But the indication always has been that Brady can criticize a call that's made during a game in his Fox role, but he can't take it to egregious levels."Notice the word subjective. It means nobody outside the league office can say exactly where the line sits.Sunday gave Brady several chances to find it. Green Bay was flagged for roughing Goff on separate plays involving Brenton Cox Jr. and Karl Brooks, and Brady had objections to both. On the late flag against Brooks, he sounded baffled."No, my goodness! What is that?" he said. "You can't keep tacking on 15 yards."That reads as a man reacting to a play, not attacking the people who made the call. FOX rules analyst Dean Blandino backed Brady's assessment of that tackle, which helps his case.What happened the last time he pushed backThe league has been here before. In November 2024, Brady questioned Brian Branch's ejection during another Packers-Lions game, and the NFL took no disciplinary action.NFL spokesperson Brian McCarthy said then that the concern was excessive criticism or comments questioning an official's integrity.Those are two clear markers. Heat alone does not seem to be the test. Questioning integrity is. Going by what has been reported, Brady's Sunday comments were about whether specific flags were right, not about whether anyone was acting in bad faith.The awkwardness comes with the job. FOX wants Brady to explain what he sees, and viewers expect a straight answer when a replay makes a penalty hard to follow. The ownership stake adds a second audience in the league office. Every sharp line gets read twice.So far, no flag has come from the league office. Until one does, Brady's Sunday stays on the safe side of a line only the league can see.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dan Lanning won't speculate on Dante Moore's potential 2027 return
articles.summary: The announcement of Dante Moore not returning to the field raises questions on his future, but Dan Lanning chose not to speculate on any next moves.
articles.body:
The announcement of Dante Moore not returning to the field for the Oregon Ducks in 2026 isn't a complete surprise. The hit he took on Sept. 26 against the USC Trojans was each of the following: scary, dangerous and uncalled for. Moore and his inner circle making the decision to protect his health is an understandable one, even if Oregon remained in national title contention, which they most certainly aren't.

The decision also raises some significant questions.

Will Moore enter the 2027 NFL Draft? He cited increasing his preparedness for the pros as one of the main reasons he opted to return to Eugene despite being a potential top-5 pick last spring. He took part in just two full games this fall, as he didn't play the second half in Week 3 against Portland State and exited early in the second quarter against USC.

Is a return to Oregon on the table? Despite potentially losing a third of its starters to the NFL, the Ducks should return a talented core, assuming there aren't major losses to the transfer portal.

And in the modern age of college football, it's impossible to rule out a transfer elsewhere for Moore, though he's been incredibly loyal to Oregon. Amid an offensive coordinator turnover, would Moore be better off playing at a different program and heading into the 2028 NFL Draft?

Right now, it's all speculation — and nothing that Lanning was willing to touch on during his press conference on Monday night when asked about Moore potentially returning to Oregon in 2027.

"That's not fair for me to say or speculate. Obviously, he'll have a decision again at the end of the season of what that looks like," Lanning said. "I think we all can acknowledge that Dante's a great player, and he'll get the opportunity to be drafted. But what that looks like in the future, I think that's a decision for a later date. I don't know where his mind's at on that. We haven't had that conversation. That's not where my focus is at, or his. I don't think that's where his focus is at right now. There's a reason you get time to be able to make that decision."

On the heels of 2025, a season in which Moore completed 71.8% of his passes for 3,565 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions, the former five-star was widely considered to be the No. 2 quarterback prospect in the draft, falling behind only Indiana Hoosiers standout and Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza. Behind the Las Vegas Raiders in the draft order, who took Mendoza first overall, was the New York Jets, also in need of a young passer to hang their hat on.

Moore spurned the draft, and potentially the Jets, instead turning his attention towards returning to college football with the Ducks. Now, after an uneven start to the 2026 season that included a clear disconnect with his pass catchers in a Week 2 loss to Oklahoma State, Moore has dropped all the way to No. 37 in longtime ESPN draft analyst Mel Kiper Jr.'s 2027 big board . While there's some debate to be had, and Kiper certainly doesn't represent the opinion of all league personnel, he falls behind five other quarterbacks on the big board: Drew Mestemaker (Oklahoma State), Trinidad Chambliss (Ole Miss), Darian Mensah (Miami), CJ Carr (Notre Dame) and Austin Simmons (Missouri).

Whatever way you look at it, the return to Oregon has not gone anywhere near as planned for Moore. What's next for his future remains a question that may not be answered for awhile, possibly months — but it's one that will have ripple effects on Oregon football for years to come.
